analysis.data_caveats: The dataset spans mostly 2020-2023 for detailed investment records and 2024-2026 for economic indicators, with a thin and recent (July 2026) burst of GDELT news-derived investment/humanitarian signals that lack the granularity of the AidData/WorldBankPPI records; direct comparability across time periods is therefore limited.

<parameter name="trend_summary">The Cameroon dataset is dominated by investment/development-finance activity (225 of 321 total events, ~70%), overwhelmingly tied to Chinese state financiers (Unspecified Chinese Government Institution, China Ministry of Commerce, China Eximbank, Chinese Embassy) engaging with Cameroonian government recipient agencies, alongside a smaller but active World Bank PPI private-sector infrastructure channel (energy, transport). Conflict and political-violence-targeting-civilians categories are very thin (2 events each) and appear to be GDELT-parsed news snippets with ambiguous or possibly mis-attributed content rather than clear security incidents. Macroeconomic indicators show a moderate, fairly stable picture: real GDP growth ~3.1-3.3% (2025-2026, IMF), inflation ~3.4-3.5% (2025-2026), government debt declining slightly from 40.4% to 39.3% of GDP (2025-2026, IMF), but a current account deficit widening from -3.3% (2024, WorldBank) to a projected -5.1% (2026, IMF). Recent (July 2026) GDELT-sourced items point to active new investment agreements (CFA 20.5 billion, businessincameroon.com, 2026-07-01) and a U.S. health-infrastructure donation (CFA 6 billion in mobile field hospitals, businessincameroon.com, 2026-07-01), suggesting continued diversification of external partners beyond China. Overall, the pattern is one of sustained multilateral/bilateral development engagement with limited, ambiguous unrest signal in this data window.
